(1) object detection embeddings are not suitable for content-based image search, (2) the object detection framework is a suitable tool for extracting discriminative image embeddings, and (3) our proposed guided training paradigm is an effective way to learn discriminative object embeddings.

(1) the discriminative power for image retrieval of embeddings extracted from object detection models is worse than that of classification models, (2) object detection models can be used as a hard attention mechanism to focus on salient regions in the convolutional feature maps, and (3) guided student-teacher learning can be used to efficiently extract object-level features from convolutional feature maps.
